page.overview:
What is Menegroth?

Menegroth, also known as the Thousand Caves or Caves of Menegroth, was the capital city of Doriath, which was home to King Thingol and Queen Melian of the Sindarin people during the First Age.

Within it was the beautifully decorated Menelrond where Thingol's throne sat, and where he dispensed his judgments and eventually would be slain in FA 502. In the Ruin of Doriath, the caves were taken by the Sons of Fëanor in their pursuit of one of the Silmarils prior to the War of Wrath.

In the years after the Battle of the Powers, the Teleri were scattered throughout Beleriand in havens such as Falas or in forests of Region and Neldoreth. Their leader Elwë disappeared for a long time, in the woods with Melian, his beloved. Then, he reappeared with Melian, calling himself Thingol, and was urged to build a home for his people. He had the Dwarves of Belegost aid in the construction of a new fortress, dug into the western wall of the ravine above the river Esgalduin, and with only one entrance, high above the river, accessible by a great bridge of stone. It was named Menegroth or the Thousand Caves because of the extensive number of caverns and chambers, all of hewn stone, and beautifully decorated with carvings of beech trees and birds. These places included armories, treasures, smithies, and living quarters for both the Elves and Dwarves.

Menegroth and Doriath enjoyed peace for a long time as Thingol preferred isolation, ordering his people not to meddle in the affairs of the Ñoldor due to the Kinslaying at Alqualondë, and the Quenya language was forbidden in his realm. Only with his kin in Nargothrond did Thingol remain in contact. He took no part in the later Battles of Beleriand relating to the struggle with Morgoth.
